Name: Antifungal Hydrosol Blend
Ingredients: Lavender Hydrosol; Solubol
Directions:
Choose 4–5 essential oils for this blend.

Step 1: Search the Component Database for two variables: antifungal and monoterpenols. Go to search on the left-hand navigation, choose antifungal from the therapeutic property list on the right, and monoterpenol for the chemical family on the left, then click the red search button.

Step 2: Read all the component datasheets that your search results show.

Step 3: Search on Aromatics International for the oils high those components from your search

Step 4: Choose 4–5 oils for your antifungal spray. Use a total of approximately 30 drops of essential oil in the 2 oz spray (3% dilution).

Step 5: Add 4 drops of Solubol* for each drop of essential oil used. If you use 30 drops of essential oils, how much solubol? Yup, 120 drops. I know, it is a lot, but that is what it takes for the solubol to blend the essential oil into the water. If you have a small graduated cylinder that measures by the ml (milliliter) use that and add 6 ml, rather than counting 120 drops! (There are about 20 drops per ml.)

Step 6: Make your label. You can create a name for the blend, or put the ingredients on the label, or both.
Notes:
Note on shelf life: This blend is water-based (hydrosol) and doesn't contain any preservatives, so you'll want to make a fresh bottle every few weeks. Be sure to read the All About Preservatives and Antioxidants reference page.

 

* Solubol: As you know, essential oils and water do not mix. When essential oils are added into a water or hydrosol spray, the tiny droplets of essential oil stay separate from the water/hydrosol. When sprayed on the body we get tiny droplets of neat essential oil on our skin. To evenly disperse essential oil into the water/hydrosol we use "Solubol.” It works great to protect the skin from neat essential oil and has a very mild aroma that doesn't seem to influence the aroma of the blend. We use Solubol in sprays we make for damaged or sensitive skin, not for the average spray blend.

There is some debate about how much Solubol one needs to fully disperse essential oil into the water. The range seems to go from 1:1 ratio (1 drop Solubol to 1 drop essential oil), to 1:8 (8 drops Solubol to 1 drop essential oil). The folks we buy it from use it at a 1:4 ratio (1 drop essential oil to 4 drops Solubol). Aromatics International's Solubol is made in France. It has a 2-year shelf life.

It is an all-natural product, here are the ingredients:

Sucrose Stearate – An emulsifier made from sugar and vegetable oil
Helianthus annus – Annual sunflower oil
Cera alba – Beeswax
Sterculia urens – a medium-sized, deciduous tree that exudes a gum called karaya used in food as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener
The gum of the acacia tree
Propolis Wax from bees
Purpose: Make an Antifungal Hydrosol Spray blend

Name: Pomegranate Seed Body Butter
Ingredients: Shea butter; Coconut Oil ; Cocoa Butter; Pomegranate Seed Oil
Directions:
4 oz Shea Butter
2 oz Coconut Oil
1 oz Cocoa Butter
1 oz Pomegranate Seed Oil 

Melt the cocoa butter over low heat until almost liquefied using a double boiler.
Add the shea butter and coconut oil until the mixture completely melts.
Once these oils are melted together, add the pomegranate seed oil.
Cover and place this mixture in the refrigerator for about 30 - 90 minutes until partially cooled. The blend should be stirrable but not liquid. 
Remove cooled oils from the refrigerator. Using a hand-held emulsion blender or electric mixer, whip the mixture until it is the desired consistency. It should be beautifully light and fluffy! 
Pour into 2 oz glass jars, and enjoy!
Purpose: This luscious whipped body butter is packed full of healthy nutrients that will leave your skin feeling moisturized and happy! Perfect for areas that need extra attention such as hands, feet, knees, and elbows.
